Subject: Clarify localized storage commitment in DPA — potential transient syncs

Hi Sofia,

Quick follow-up as we review the DPA for our deployment: Acme Health requires that all patient-related payloads for EU-resident subjects be stored and processed within the EU. Our legal team is seeing a DPA clause that references "region affinity" rather than a hard lock. Before we move forward, can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood can contractually guarantee EU-only storage for Primary Data (artefacts tied to EU subjects), and 2) whether temporary, timeboxed syncs to the US for back-office analytics/aggregation are supported (we've been quoted a window of up to 72 hours in some conversations).

If temporary syncs are allowed, we need details on: retention limits, encryption (KMS), subprocessors that would have access during the window, and audit proof (who/when/what).

Please advise whether you have a standard addendum or language we can use in the DPA. We may need a short call with product + security to walk through the controls.

Thanks,
Anna Perez
Head of Security Operations

Hi team —

High level: we should avoid a blanket "hard lock" language that claims zero cross-border processing under all operational circumstances (this introduces operational fragility and blocks replication/DR). Instead, we can offer a contractual "EU-primary residency with timeboxed transient sync" addendum that meets Acme's needs while giving us safe operational guardrails. Suggested guardrails:

- Scope: Define Primary Data types (PII, patient records) that are covered by the residency guarantee. Non-primary telemetry (service metrics, anonymized telemetry) excluded.
- Timeboxed syncs: Allow explicit transient replication for analytics/aggregation with a configurable maximum window (suggest default 24 hours; allow up to 72h only with explicit customer approval and documented justification).
- Encryption: Data must be encrypted in transit and at rest. For any transient sync, customer-managed KMS keys are required (bring-your-own-key).
- Access controls: Subprocessors with potential exposure must be enumerated and restricted to roles that cannot de-anonymize cached payloads; access via RBAC + just-in-time ephemeral credentials.
- Auditability: Every transient replication must emit an audit event with tenant id, dataset id, replication start/end, and operators involved. Audit logs must be retained per contract (e.g., 2 years or per customer request).
- Notification & approval: Customer must be notified in advance for any scheduled bulk sync; emergency/incident-driven syncs require post-facto notification within 24 hours and a documented justification.

Attached: draft addendum (dpa-eu-localization-addendum-v1.pdf) and current subprocessors roster (subprocessors_2025-10-06.csv). Please review operational implications, Karthik.

If Acme confirms 24h window we can sign faster; if they insist on 72h we'll need a legal review plus further controls (e.g., additional encryption, limited operator set).

— Marissa

Sofia / Marissa — operational notes below. TL;DR: technically feasible with the platform features we have, with a couple of implementation steps and some telemetry changes.

Feasibility/Mechanics:
- Region affinity: We can ensure primary tenancy and storage in the EU region by tenant tagging and storage policies.
- Transient syncs: Implement as timeboxed replication jobs that create ephemeral copies in a US analytics cluster; those copies are single-tenant scoped, encrypted with the customer's KMS, and have a TTL enforcement that triggers irreversible deletion after the agreed window.
- KV cache and model hot-shard: Ensure cache keys are scoped to EU tenancy; any KV export must go through the same replication job with audit hooks.

Controls to require in the addendum:
- Default window of 24h; allow 72h only if customer explicitly checks a box and approves additional controls (evidence of aggregated-only usage, no raw re-identifiable exports).
- Enforce BYOK (customer-managed KMS) for temporary copies. If customer declines BYOK, limit window to 8 hours and require stricter operator approvals.
- Automated audit events: replication.start, replication.complete, replication.delete with tenant id and job id. Ops will surface a daily digest to the customer's security mailbox.
- Subprocessor isolation: Only specific US analytics subprocessors will be in the list; we need legal vetting of the current roster (see Marissa's attachment).

Ops timeline & runbook: we have a templated runbook (ops-runbook_geofence_sync.md) that covers deployment steps, rollbacks, and deletion verification. I recommend a staged pilot with one dataset and a 24-hour window.

Happy to walk them through the runbook on the call.

— Karthik

Hi Anna / Acme team —

Thanks for the patience. Summary of what Redwood can offer based on internal review:

1) Contractual stance: We will provide an EU-primary residency guarantee for defined Primary Data types. That guarantee is operationalized via tenant tagging and EU-region storage. This will be captured in the DPA addendum (see attached draft).

2) Transient syncs: We can support timeboxed transient replication to US analytics clusters under the following default terms: 24-hour window (customer may request up to 72 hours but that triggers additional controls and review).

3) Mandatory controls for any transient replication: customer-managed KMS (BYOK), explicit pre-scheduled notification for planned bulk jobs, post-facto notification for emergency/incident-driven syncs, automated audit events retained per contract, and a limit on which subprocessors may access the transient copies.

4) Next steps:
- Please review the attached DPA addendum (dpa-eu-localization-addendum-v1.pdf) and the subprocessors roster.
- Confirm whether Acme will accept the default 24-hour window or requests 72 hours and a short justification.
- Provide the legal contact for signature (we will generate the DocuSign link once we have sign-off).
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough of the ops runbook and pilot plan.
